checks.root_repairs: Canonicalized every artifact path; replaced six stale work pins for Item407 by five audited canonical pins; narrowed the draft's broad method-class language to an audit of the explicitly named mechanisms; and corrected the conditional direct-margin notation to j=(d-g)_+.

mathematical_audit.support_carrier: After removing the exact common divisors from the triple-minor packet and actual target residual, the rejection condition is p dividing Pi_sat but not Gamma_sat. Therefore the integer carrier J=(Pi_sat)_(Gamma_sat) has exactly the required prime support on compatible rows.
mathematical_audit.target_branch_split: When the distinguished coefficient f is nonzero, the target reduces to the declared incomplete-period scalar residual; when f is zero, it reduces to the vector residual 9*4^s*b-11*v. The split preserves the actual target rather than an ambient packet.
mathematical_audit.finite_witness_scope: For (p,r,s,M)=(709,347,2,885), the exact values Pi=Pi_sat=79, Gamma=Gamma_sat=1 and J=79 refute the all-row integer identities Pi_sat=1 and J=1. Since 79 is foreign to the tied prime 709, the row proves no asymptotic density statement.
mathematical_audit.screened_mechanisms: The five displayed gauges of the known gate operator, bounded propagation, matched common-divisor resultants, matched-factor atomicity and pointwise height do not yield a positive lower bound for tied-prime support of J. This conclusion is deliberately restricted to those mechanisms and is not an exhaustive information-class impossibility theorem.
mathematical_audit.capacity_coupling: If J_e(M)>=jM+o(M), D(M)>=dM+o(M), G(M)<=gM+o(M) and N(M)<=nM+o(M), Item407 gives normalized one-ray saving max(0,j,1/35-g-n)/6. Under the direct margin D-G, one may take j=(d-g)_+. None of the audited inputs proves a positive margin.
mathematical_audit.smallest_missing_lemma: A formula-specific tied large-prime Smith anti-gcd theorem J_e(M)>=delta*M+o(M) on one selected fixed-M ray remains the smallest actual-family lemma capable of activating the rejection chart.
